description.narrative: The project will demonstrate economically competitive, environmentally sustainable and socially inclusive development for Vinh Yen city (Vinh Yen), Hue city (Hue) and Ha Giang city (Ha Giang) of Viet Nam. The project cities' green and climate resilient development approaches will be scaled up for nationwide green secondary city development in Viet Nam.

Frequency of flood events in the Hue Citadel Progress/Status: Not yet due
The flood occurred on October 15, 2022. The peak flooding on the Huong River was +3.98m, which did not affect three completed inner-city roads (Ong Ich Khiem, Ton That Thiep, Xuan 68). The post-flood inundation has been mitigated. The remaining flooding time is about 1.5 days. Hence, 0.5 days have been reduced. Data Source: Ha Giang, Hue, and Vinh Yen project progress reports Baseline value: Once every 2 years

Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Green and resilient urban infrastructure services in Ha Giang improved Indicator: Kilometers of embankments along the Lo and Mien rivers and Me stream protected, and the river courses rehabilitated Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Not yet achieved -1km embankment and landscaping west of Lo river (CW04): The contract was signed, but construction has not yet commenced due to the revision of the DED, the updating of the cost estimate, and the compensation plan. After the storm events in 2024 with extremely high rainfall intensity caused severe flooding in Ha Giang city, PPC has recently required the Department of Agriculture and Environment (DAE) to reassess and identify any potential negative impacts that may be caused if the sections are embanked in the downstream waterway of the Lo River. By 6 January 2026, Tuyen Quang PPC sent official letter to ADB proposed cancelling this component/investment due to negative impacts identified from its study. - 3km embankment and landscaping of the Mien River (CW06): the contractor has resumed the work after loans were extended, progress at 22%. - 1.6 km embankment of the south and landscaping of the Me river (CW05): The updated FS, followed by DED, was re-approved in November 2024 after ADB had no objection to enhancing the green design features. The bidding document was submitted and approved in October 2025. The advertisement was in November 2025. The BER is under preparation/review. The contract award aims for Q3/2026.
Data Source: Ha Giang project progress report

Output: Green and resilient urban infrastructure services in Ha Giang improved Indicator: Kilometers of urban drainage channels in the Minh Khai, Nguyen Trai, Quang Trung, and Tran Phu wards upgraded or rehabilitated Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Not yet achieved.
CW01: This package was on a post-review basis, and its original scope was to construct 13 sewer lines. However, due to the very high cost re-estimated during the DMS stage, the land acquisition cost was extremely high compared to the estimated initially, and the contract could not be awarded, even after the bid evaluation result (BER) was completed. The updated FS was re-approved to reduce to 6 sewer lines of 4.85km (reduced 2.15km from 7.0 km initially designed). The revised PP was approved in June 2025, the package was advertised in December 2025. BER is under preparation and aiming for the award by Q3/2026. Data Source: Ha Giang project progress report

Output: Green and resilient urban infrastructure services in Ha Giang improved Indicator: Kilometers of urban roads constructed Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Not yet achieved - 2.1 km Phung Hung road (CW07) is completed. Handed over for use in July 2025. - 2.9 km of the southern ring road (CW03): Contract was awarded. Construction commenced with progress of about 25% due to severely affected by Typhoons in Oct 2025. - 1.2 km of the National highway 2 and bridge works (CW02): The construction site was handed over in Oct 2023. Construction progress achieved at 42%, as it was disrupted by typhoon events in 2025, caused landslides and erosion on the right-side embankment of the project route. Contracts of CW02/03 were impacted with some work items need to be redone. The Project Management Unit has coordinated with relevant provincial departments and agencies, reported the extent of the damage, and submitted proposed remedial measures to the Provincial People's Committee and ADB. The DED of additional work is under preparation and expected to be completed in Feb/Mar, then VOs will follow. Data Source: Ha Giang project progress report

19 Government professionals (with 04 females, 21%) attended the training. Data Source: Ha Giang project progress report

Data Source: Ha Giang project progress report

Output: Green and resilient urban infrastructure services in Ha Giang improved Indicator: Number of streetlights replaced with energy-efficient streetlights Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Not yet achieved The original bidding process was canceled because no qualified bidder. The PMU is updating the DED, cost estimate and draft BD for re-bidding. The advertisement will be in Q2/2026 and contract award aims for Q3/2026. Data Source: Ha Giang project progress report

Output: Green and resilient urban infrastructure services in Hue improved Indicator: Number of government staff (at least 33% women) in the executing and implementing agencies who gain new project management skills on procurement, safeguards, social and gender, public finance, and anticorruption measures Achievement: 4 Progress/Status: Achieved.
103 government staff, of which 38 were female (36.9%), were trained on project management, safeguards, social and gender aspects, and GAP
For the training activity, the project has implemented 05 training courses for project staff and related staff on safeguards policies, monitoring and evaluation, financial/contract management, community supervision, and more within the scope of HU-CS01 Consultant. 142 staff members from PPMU, Departments, People's Committees of wards/communes, and contractor representatives were trained, of which 48 were female, accounting for 33.8%.
Under the Community-led Initiative component, the HU-CS03 consultant and the contractor also conducted 185 training sessions/classes on 04 topics (Community-based Disaster Risk Management; communication on Epidemics and Environmental Sanitation; Disaster Response Skills; extracurricular on Climate Change and Disaster Risk in Schools) for 5,163 attendants, with a female ratio of about 60.3% (3,113 attendants).
Data Source: Hue project progress report
